identification_clues: The adult has seven black spots on red wing covers. The larva is long, dark, and spiny with orange patches. The two life stages look different but belong to the same species.
adaptations_ecology: Adults and larvae eat aphids on plants. By feeding on these small plant-eating insects, ladybugs help protect garden plants. Both life stages can find food among leaves and stems.

identification_clues: This slender lizard can be green or brown. It has a pointed head, a long tail, and gripping toe pads. A male may extend a pink throat fan called a dewlap.
adaptations_ecology: Toe pads help the anole climb stems, branches, and fences. It hunts insects and spiders among plants. The male uses its throat fan to communicate with other anoles.

identification_clues: This upright plant has alternate leaves. Each palmately compound leaf has narrow leaflets arranged like fingers. Blue, pea-shaped flowers grow in a cluster called a raceme.
adaptations_ecology: A low, leafy rosette grows before the flower stalk. The plant flowers in spring in sunny, open places. Its flowers provide food for visiting insects.

size: Spreading stems up to 25 cm (10 in) long
identification_clues: This low plant has spreading stems and rough, pointed leaves in whorls of four to six. Tiny pink-lilac flowers have four lobes and grow in small, leafy clusters.
adaptations_ecology: Field madder is an introduced annual that grows in lawns and open, disturbed ground. Its spreading stems form a low patch among grass blades. It completes its life cycle within one year.
